$comment: THE WIDTH-VIEW OPERAND MODIFIER, RUNNABLE ON BOTH CPUs (D-CSUBSET-INLINE-ASM-OPERANDS; tranche 2 of D-ASM-BARE-OPERAND-WIDTH-DIVERGES-FROM-REFERENCE). ★★★ THE FORM WAS A REFUSAL UNTIL 2026-08-24 — `error[S0067] the inline-asm template uses the operand modifier '%w'` — so this example could not have been written at all before the dialects declared `assembly.templateModifiers`. ★★★ WHAT MAKES IT A TEST RATHER THAN A SMOKE RUN: every assertion reads ABOVE BIT 31. ✔MEASURED that the same program written through `(int)` exits 42 whether the move was 32-bit or 64-bit — the truncation destroys exactly the evidence — so the seed's two halves differ (`0x11223344` / `0x55667788`) and shape 6 asserts that the `(int)` observation IS blind, rather than leaving a reader to assume the wide checks were merely thorough. ★★ BOTH DECLARED LETTERS ARE ASSERTED on each dialect (`%w`/`%x` on aarch64, `%k`/`%q` on x86-64) because the two failure modes are opposite: a build ignoring the letter passes every wide shape and fails every narrow one, and a build hard-coding 'a modifier means 32' does the reverse. ⚠ THE `release` ARM IS NOT DECORATION — a `volatile` seed plus the optimizer is what witnesses that the template survives the shipped pipeline; a release-only miscompile has shipped in this project before.
